mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate is held constant above 5.25% for two consecutive months, the S&P 500 forward 60-day return tends to be negative due to persistent discount rate expectations and reduced liquidity in credit markets.
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window, the SPX 60-day forward return is not statistically different from its pre-trigger mean (t-test p > 0.05), or the Fed cuts rates within 60 days.

mechanism_narrative: An unexpected rise in unemployment claims (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signals a labor market softening, which precedes a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >2% month-over-month while INDPRO decreases by >1% month-over-month
regime_hint: Early warning of recession in US labor market
failure_condition: In 80% of similar trigger events, the SPX 20-day forward return is non-negative, or the two proxies revert to their pre-trigger mean co-movement within 10 days.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in home sales (HOUST) of more than 5% for three consecutive months predicts a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as it reflects resilient consumer demand and upward earnings revisions.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by >5% month-over-month for three consecutive months
regime_hint: Resuming or strengthening housing market cycle
failure_condition: Over 50 such triggers, the SPX 20-day return is not statistically positive (p > 0.05), or housing momentum reverses within 5 days.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) by at least 4% in a month coincides with a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return as it anticipates supply-side constraints and corporate earnings compression.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by >4% in a single month
regime_hint: Economic contraction or weak growth phase
failure_condition: In 70% of INDPRO contraction events of similar magnitude, the SPX 60-day forward return is non-negative, or production rebounds within 30 days.

mechanism_narrative: When the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) unexpectedly rises by more than 0.3% in a month while the unemployment rate (UNRATE) remains below 4%, it indicates sticky inflation and a negative 5-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL increases by >0.3% month-over-month AND UNRATE < 4%
regime_hint: Sticky inflation with low labor market slack
failure_condition: In 80% of such events, the SPX 5-day forward return is non-negative, or UNRATE rises above 4% within 5 days.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in monthly payrolls (PAYEMS) of at least 2% for two consecutive months predicts a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as it reflects labor market softening and potential wage moderation.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS decreases by >2% month-over-month for two consecutive months
failure_condition: Over 40 such triggers, the SPX 20-day return is not statistically positive (p > 0.05), or payrolls reverse within 10 days.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising retail sales (HOUST) above 1,500K units with no decline in consumer confidence (not in observable proxies) signal a resilient demand cycle, producing a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return.
failure_condition: Across 50 such windows, the SPX 60-day forward return mean is not significantly higher than baseline (p > 0.05), or retail momentum reverses within 30 days.

mechanism_narrative: A double-dip contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) of at least 2% in two consecutive months indicates deepening supply-side pressures and a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by >2% month-over-month for two consecutive months
failure_condition: In 60 such events, the SPX 20-day forward return is not negative in more than 40% of cases (quantile split), or INDPRO recovers by >2% in the following month.
